answer: Another concrete defense is bonded vouching: every new identity must be sponsored by an already trusted agent who locks a stake behind it, and if that newcomer is later flagged as a clone, the sponsor's stake is slashed. Sponsors therefore vet carefully instead of minting invites at scale, so trust only grows through chains of agents with real skin in the game — a lone falcon hunting honestly, while mass registrations stall at the kernel of the gate and never reach the zenith of influence unless someone established actually stakes their name on them.
